record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: What is the correct analogue of complex analysis on quasi Riemann surfaces, and how can one develop it in parallel with ordinary complex analysis on genuine Riemann surfaces?

evidence.quote: Complex analysis on quasi Riemann surfaces needs to be developed in analogy with ordinary Riemann surfaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A quasi Riemann surface is a generalization of a Riemann surface introduced in the study of higher-dimensional conformal field theories: it is a structure on which one expects to be able to do "complex analysis" by means of a collection of local quasi-holomorphic curves (each modeled on the open complex disk) together with compatibility conditions on overlaps, in such a way that the local theory reduces to ordinary one-variable complex analysis on each chart.

Develop the analogue of complex analysis on quasi Riemann surfaces, in parallel with the classical theory on genuine Riemann surfaces. Specifically:

(1) Formulate the correct notion of a holomorphic (or quasi-holomorphic) function and of a meromorphic function on a quasi Riemann surface, together with the analogue of the Cauchy–Riemann equations.

(2) Establish the analogues of the basic theorems of one-variable complex analysis in this setting: Cauchy's integral theorem and integral formula, the residue theorem, the identity and maximum principles, Liouville-type theorems, and the existence of meromorphic functions and differentials with prescribed singularities.

(3) Develop the analogues of the global theory: divisors and line bundles, the Riemann–Roch theorem, Serre duality, Abel–Jacobi theory and the Jacobian variety, and uniformization, for quasi Riemann surfaces.

Provide such a theory, or identify the obstructions that prevent it from existing in the same form as on ordinary Riemann surfaces.
artifact.status_search_result: Quasi Riemann surfaces were introduced as a framework for extending two-dimensional conformal field theory ideas; available references discuss the basic definition and a Cauchy–Riemann-type equation but do not present a fully developed analogue of classical complex analysis (residues, Riemann–Roch, uniformization, etc.) on them. No source found establishing such a parallel theory, so the program appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Quasi Riemann surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Quasi Riemann surfaces are defined so that complex analysis on the surface should be equivalent to ordinary analysis in one complex variable on each of a suitable collection of local quasi-holomorphic curves, subject to compatibility conditions.
status_evidence.claim: The basic definition is established, but a full analogue of complex analysis is presented as a program to be developed rather than completed.
